10.1002_smll.76257: The increasing demand for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) attracts sustainable recycling, particularly for high‐value metals such as Ni and Co used in high‐Ni ternary cathodes. However, current hydrometallurgical processes rely on multistage solvent extractions that exhibit poor Ni selectivity and generate large quantities of Na 2 SO 4 waste because of extensive pH adjustment and extractant saponification. Herein, we report an organocatalyst‐inspired, sulfur‐donor extractants (TPA‐H) designed through molecular‐level engineering for highly selective direct Ni recovery. These P(V)‐based extractants enable direct and efficient Ni extraction under strongly acidic conditions (pH ∼0.5), achieving an exceptional Ni/Co separation factor (β) exceeding 2300. Mechanistic studies revealed that the optimized structure and coordination of the phosphorodithioate framework preferentially stabilize Ni(II) over competing metals. Large‐scale extractions using real spent LIB black mass leachates demonstrated >95% Ni extraction efficiency under acidic conditions. Subsequent stripping and recrystallization without an intermediate scrubbing step afforded high‐purity NiSO 4 ·6H 2 O (99.7%), while suppressing Na 2 SO 4 byproduct generation. The TPA‐Hs exhibited excellent recyclability over 10 consecutive cycles, and the recovered Ni was directly crystallized as high‐purity NiSO 4 ·6H 2 O. Furthermore, integration of an advanced‐flow reactor (AFR)–Zaiput separator platform enabled biphasic mass transfer, thereby overcoming the limitations of mixer–settler systems and facilitating automated continuous extraction–separation processes.
10.1021_acsami.6c03202: Much remains to be understood about the chemical environment of the battery anode’s solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) under operando conditions. The challenge partly arises because the main technique for SEI composition analysis, room temperature X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (RT-XPS), is confounded by the severe SEI evolution that occurs through reactions and volatilization during RT-XPS. A recent technical breakthrough is our introduction of cryo-XPS for battery research, which uses instant plunge freezing to ensure operando- relevant interface preservation during XPS measurements. Yet uncertainty remains about which sample preparation protocol best reflects operando -relevant chemical speciation during ex situ XPS. Importantly, this work establishes that due to the surface-sensitive nature of XPS, sample preparation becomes crucial during characterization. Here, cryo-XPS is utilized as a convenient tool to identify the differences arising from different sample preparation protocols. We show that the controlled, rinse-dried cryo-sample (d-SEI) provides a more accurate representation of the operando -relevant SEI chemical composition. This is the preferred protocol because not only does d-SEI ensure probe depth certainty, unlike the unwashed blotted SEI (w-SEI), but it also reveals more buried species during cryo-XPS.
10.1021_acsnano.5c17322: Aqueous Zn//V 2 O 5 batteries (ZVBs) hold promise for large-scale energy storage due to their high safety and low cost, but face critical challenges of Zn dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions at the Zn anode, coupled with severe vanadium dissolution and shuttle at the V 2 O 5 cathode. Conventional strategies, such as electrolyte engineering or separator modifications, often focus on single-component optimization, neglecting synergistic anode and cathode regulation. Herein, we developed a Zeolite Socony Mobil-5 (ZSM-5) filled glass fiber separator (ZSM-5@GF) to address these issues simultaneously. The ZSM-5 zeolite facilitates the Zn 2+ desolvation via binding H 2 O molecules, suppressing HER and side reactions. And it could also homogenize the ion concentration distribution for dendrite-free Zn plating/stripping. Concurrently, ZSM-5 zeolite could also immobilize dissolved vanadium species via electrostatic adsorption, mitigating cathode degradation and shuttle-induced capacity fading. Benefiting from the synergistic anode/cathode interface regulation, both electrodes dramatically extended their cycle life, and an Ah-level pouch-type Zn//V 2 O 5 cell is also realized for continuous cycling. This bifunctional separator realizes synergistic stabilization of the Zn anode and V 2 O 5 cathode, offering a cost-effective and scalable strategy for high-performance AZVBs toward practical applications.
10.1109_tcsi.2026.3652828: Battery-free tags offer a power-efficient solution for the wireless connection in Internet of Things (IoT), where the backscatter communication that is compatible with widely-deployed protocols such as Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) significantly reduces the hardware cost thanks to the seamless integration into the existing infrastructure. However, there are three main shortcomings in the existing battery-free BLE tags: 1)The tag-to-access point (AP, uplink) communication ranges are limited to 97 meters at -10dBm incident power, which are not long enough for some outdoor scenes. 2) The AP-to-tag (downlink) communication in the state of the arts has not exceeded a 1Mbps data rate and a 4m range, disabling remote tag configuration. 3)The tag-to-tag communication has not been realized in a battery-free way, which cannot construct a passive IoT network. In this work, we demonstrate an integrated bidirectional passive BLE chip that conducts battery-free BLE communication in tag-to-tablet/smartphone, tablet/smartphone-to-tag, and tag-to-tag modes. The chip is implemented in a 65nm CMOS process. An all-digital intermediate frequency (IF) shaping technique is proposed to extend the tag-to-tablet/smartphone (uplink) communication range to 160m at$7.16\mu $W power consumption and a -10dBm incident tone. In addition, a$2^{nd}$-order intermodulation (IM2) based charge-domain GFSK demodulation technique is proposed to enable 1Mbps 12m downlink communication at$6.8\mu $W power consumption, which realizes both tablet/smartphone-to-tag and tag-to-tag communication in a fully battery-free way. As a result, the bidirectional passive BLE chip offers a potential solution for future battery-free IoT mesh network.
